timing.label: Slack update to the support lead (≤120 words, spoken in 90 s)
Objection 1 (technical)
timing.question: Who is accountable when the bot posts a wrong diagnosis?

timing.label: Objection 2 (commercial)
timing.question: My team will stop reading the channel if the bot posts every time.

problem.quote: So I set up a responder, basically a Support and Bugs one

approach.quote: It groups the double-charge reports into one issue linked to the first thread

evidence.quote: Actually, the replay had six posts

must_mention.point: Repeated double-charge reports are grouped into one issue linked to the first report's thread, not answered each time
must_mention.evidence_quote: It groups the double-charge reports into one issue linked to the first thread, so it does not answer each time

must_mention.point: A shared scratchpad keeps triaged reports with channel, timestamp and reporter, the duplicates and the routing table
must_mention.evidence_quote: it keeps the triaged reports with channel and timestamp and reporter, the duplicates and the routing table

must_mention.point: A routing correction replied in the thread updates the routing table so later reports go to the right owner
The diagnosis is written back once in the original thread with the owner tagged, and repeats only get a reaction
must_mention.evidence_quote: The diagnosis is written back once in the original thread with the owner tagged, and repeats only get a reaction

must_mention.point: Channel messages are untrusted input, so the responder runs under a network policy allowlist that blocks other hosts
The same setup runs on a Microsoft Teams channel through a Teams trigger, without private channels
must_mention.evidence_quote: It can run on a Microsoft Teams channel through a Teams trigger too, without private channels

sentences_to_rerecord: The pasted ticket was also there, basically it ignored it, you know.

accuracy.anchor: Four of six points; the routing correction and the network policy are missing, and the pasted ticket was described as "ignored". (anchors: 27–30 every point tied to a count, setting or file; 15–20 four of six; under 10 two or fewer)

structure.anchor: Opened with the setup rather than the outcome; the update has no ask. (anchors: 22–25 all parts in order; 13–17 parts present but weak; under 8 problem only)

customer_relevance.anchor: Thread answers and tagging were described, but only one count reached the support lead. (anchors: 16–20 answered in terms of what the support team sees, with counts; 10–13 some; under 6 feature talk)

brevity_and_fluency.anchor: Four segments off target, a 12-second silence at T+45 and six fillers. (anchors: 11–15 segments on target, under 1 filler/min; 6–8 two or more segments off; under 4 most segments off)

recovery.anchor: Objection 1 had no boundary or evidence; objection 2 had the boundary and one number but no offer. (anchors: 7–10 acknowledge → boundary → evidence → offer held with numbers; 4–6 partial; under 3 no pattern)

stems: "Your team will stop…" — lead the framing with the outcome before the responder type.
"When an engineer says wrong owner…" — say where the correction is kept and what happens next time.
"The setting that blocks it is…" — name the network policy instead of "it ignored it".
